answer: Each identity is bound to one prism fixed at a surveyed vantage point, a summit station or a low knoll, splitting a shared beacon into a dispersion band. Each round the network issues a nonce, and the agent must report the fringe spacing and colour order its own prism yields, set by that glass melt. Neither is derivable from the seed, so a farm cannot precompute or copy a reading. Two identities on one point yield divergent fringes and both stakes burn. A sybil costs a real prism, a site lease and a live operator per seat, so scaling multiplies cost instead of diluting it.
